items.definition:
to cause someone to become hostile
Don't antagonize the dog, or it might bite.

add caffeine to; stimulate with caffeine
I need to caffeinate before my morning meeting.

to walk with difficulty, typically because of an injury
He had to hobble home after twisting his ankle.

to make magnetic
You can magnetize a needle by rubbing it with a strong magnet.

annoy slightly
Her casual remark seemed to miff him.

make random in order or arrangement
The software can randomise the order of questions.

adjust again or in a different way
She had to readjust her schedule after the change.

search unsystematically and untidily through a mass or collection of things
She began to rummage through her bag for her keys.

burn (something) superficially or lightly
The flame singed the edges of the paper.

be silent, morose, and bad-tempered out of annoyance or disappointment
He went to his room to sulk after losing the game.

to walk with short steps, swaying from side to side
The duck began to waddle towards the pond.

to make worldwide in scope or application
Technology continues to globalize communication.

to punish or disadvantage someone for breaking a rule
The referee decided to penalise the player for a foul.

to walk heavily and slowly
He continued to plod along the muddy path.

to make clean and hygienic; disinfect
Please sanitize your hands before entering the room.

To steal money placed in one's trust
The accountant was arrested for trying to embezzle funds from the company.

to make someone feel more cheerful or hopeful
The good news helped to hearten the struggling team.

move or cause to move at a great speed, typically in a noisy or violent way
The car hurtled down the highway.

intervene on behalf of another
She tried to intercede on behalf of her friend, but the judge was firm.

To run with a long, easy stride.
The deer began to lope across the field.

to move or sway unsteadily
The child began to teeter on the edge of the curb.

to equip with computers; to automate
Many businesses are looking to computerise their operations to improve efficiency.

to twist or bend out of its normal shape
The dancer managed to contort her body into incredible positions.

to remove regulations or controls from
The government decided to deregulate the telecommunications industry.

to make or become equal
The team managed to equalise in the last minute of the game.

to caress or stroke lovingly or erotically
She gently fondled her cat's ears.

To admire or revere intensely
Many young fans idolize their favorite pop stars.
